featured_reviews.review_text:
If you're a guac lover like me, you're in for a treat! We kicked things off with the Chilaquiles Filo Cups, and let me tell you-the guac was chef's kiss! The crispy, flaky texture of filo cups made every bite a delight.

featured_reviews.review_text: The food was delicious and well-prepared, which made our dining experience enjoyable initially. However, the service was disappointing. featured_reviews.name: Viraj Khedekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a weekend lunch at Millo. The restaurant is located in the Kamala Mills compound, so getting there is pretty easy.

The ambience is great. The restaurant is well maintained, clean and beautiful. The outdoor seating should probably be avoided during the monsoon. The tables are well spaced and the music is just the right volume so you don't need to shout to talk.
The service is quick and friendly. They will explain the menu and the contents of the dishes very well. They also accommodate dietary restrictions. They charge 10% as service fee.
The menu is fully vegetarian and expansive. They mainly cover Asian, Italian, and Mexican cuisines. We started with the comforting and tasty hot and sour mini soup. The Italian Tartine was tasty, the crostini were perfect to munch on. The Chilaquiles Filo Cups were a miss, the cups were nicely crisp but the guacamole was totally bland. The udon noodles were extremely tasty and were the second best item we tasted. Mind you, the noodles portion is large (for three, I'd guess). The kitchen seems to have nailed the Asian and Italian cuisine.

Overall, the experience was largely comforting. Definitely recommended, would revisit to taste more of the large menu.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Celebrating Wins, the Bhagat Tarachand Way

After a quick visit to Siddhivinayak to celebrate a friend’s professional milestone, we were in the mood for some solid vegetarian food. Naturally, Bhagat Tarachand came to mind. With so many versions out there, we just went with the closest—Bhagat Tarachand B. And it turned out to be a fantastic choice.

They offer valet parking, which is always a plus in the city. Surprisingly, even on a Monday night, there was a 40-minute wait. That said, their waiting area is well set up—plush sofas inside, extra seating outside, and the vibe inside is vibrant and upscale. Yes, a bit noisy, but still cozy. The staff was courteous, attentive, and knew their menu well.

What We Ordered:
•	Papad Churi: A classic, and they nailed it.
•	Pav Bhaji: Flavorful, though slightly on the sweeter side for my taste.
•	Shev Tamatar Sabji: Outstanding. Comfort food at its best.
•	Veg Dehati: We were torn between this and Veg Chili Mili. The waiter recommended Dehati, and he was spot on—spicy, rich, and deeply satisfying.

To go with it:
•	Special Ghee Roti: Soft and comforting.
•	Missi Roti & Makai Roti: These missed the mark for us. Definitely had better versions elsewhere.

Final Verdict:

Despite a couple of misses, Bhagat Tarachand B lives up to its reputation. The food was rich, flavorful, and satisfying. If you’re looking for elevated vegetarian dining with a touch of tradition, it’s definitely worth a visit.

I recently visited Radhe Shyam Hotel to order food for takeaway, and the entire experience was disappointing.

When I first went to the counter to place my order, I was told to go to another counter because takeaway orders were handled there. At that counter, there wasn't even a proper menu available. Instead, I was handed a photocopied menu, which felt quite unprofessional.

After deciding what to order, I was then told to go back to the first counter to make the payment. At that point, I genuinely felt like I was playing "counter to counter" instead of ordering food.

I collected my order and left, but unfortunately, I won't be visiting this place again.

After reading some of the other reviews, I guess I should consider myself lucky that the food turned out to be good and safe to eat. That's the only reason I'm giving this place an extra star. Otherwise, based on the service experience alone, it would have been a 1-star review.

featured_reviews.name: VlogWithFurkan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited SpiceKlub to explore their newly launched menu, and it was truly an impressive experience for anyone who enjoys modern Indian fusion cuisine.
We started with their appetizers, and the Masala Pav Bagel Bites were an absolute highlight. It’s a creative take on Mumbai’s classic masala pav, served inside sesame bagels with a perfect balance of spiced onion-tomato masala, buttery chutney, and cream cheese. The flavours felt familiar yet completely elevated.
The Desi Hummus Dip was another standout dish. Unlike regular hummus, this one blends creamy chickpea hummus with bold, smoky Pindi chole flavours. The crunchy toppings and spiced oil drizzle added great texture and depth, making it a must-try for fusion lovers.
For beverages, we tried the Jamun Sour and Kanji Martini. The Jamun Sour was refreshing, tangy, and well-balanced with a hint of citrus, while the Kanji Martini offered a unique fermented flavour with mustard and kala namak notes — definitely something different and worth experiencing.
In the main course, the Hyderabadi Chilli Roast was beautifully executed. Stuffed green chillies filled with herbed goat cheese paired perfectly with the rich peanut, sesame, and coconut-based salan, offering a great balance of spice and creaminess.
The most unique part of the experience was the Bubbling Kulfi. It’s served at an extreme temperature and cannot be eaten directly, making it an interactive dessert where you mix it with add-ons before enjoying. A fun and innovative concept that stands out.
Overall, SpiceKlub truly delivers when it comes to creativity, presentation, and flavour. It’s the perfect place for anyone looking to try something different from the usual dining options in Mumbai. Highly recommended for fusion food lovers!

featured_reviews.review_text:

For starters, the Crispy Aloo Chaat Bombs were an absolute crowd-pleaser—crisp, flavourful, and beautifully balanced. The Green Goodness Kebab complemented it wonderfully, making both dishes clear winners.
The main course continued to impress. The Hyderabadi Chilli Roast Sabji introduced a refreshing twist to traditional flavours and paired excellently with the Whole Wheat Lacha Paratha and Chilli Garlic Roti. The Chelo Kebab Bowl was another highlight—an indulgent medley of corn, papad, paneer, and fragrant saffron rice, delivering a perfect harmony of sweet, rich, and crisp textures.
To conclude, the Jalebi Churros provided a creative and indulgent finale—an exceptional dessert to end the meal on a high note.

A special mention to Naveen for his attentive service and spot-on recommendations, which truly elevated the overall experience.

All in all, a must-visit destination for an unforgettable dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Amreen Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Firki -A Delightful Culinary Experience

During our recent visit to Firki restaurant, we were thoroughly impressed by every aspect of our dining experience, including the food, ambience, and attentive service.

**Food:** We opted for the fixed menu, which offered a delectable array of dishes. Starting with the refreshing Pinacolada and flavorful Manchow soup, we moved on to the standout items like perfectly baked Garlic bread, aromatic Chilli paneer, and the scrumptious Hara Bhara kebab. The Firki special paneer was a delightful surprise, complemented by a selection of assorted roti. The Triple Schezwan provided a satisfying and flavorful main course, while the Mud cake concluded our meal on a sweet and indulgent note. Each dish was expertly prepared and left a lasting impression.

**Ambience:** The ambience at Firki is inviting and pleasant. The restaurant's interior is tastefully decorated, creating a warm and welcoming atmosphere. The seating arrangement allows for both intimate dining and larger group gatherings, suitable for various occasions.

**Service:** The staff at Firki deserves special commendation for their exceptional service. They were courteous, prompt, and knowledgeable about the menu offerings. Our server provided excellent recommendations and ensured that we had a seamless dining experience from start to finish.

**Recommendations:** If you visit Firki, be sure to try their Garlic bread and Mud cake, which were definite highlights of our meal.

Overall, Firki restaurant surpassed our expectations with its delicious food, inviting ambience, and attentive service. We highly recommend this establishment for anyone looking to enjoy a memorable dining experience. We look forward to returning to Firki soon!

featured_reviews.name: Prithvish Ashar
featured_reviews.review_text:
RIso - Vegetarian Delight
Owners and chefs have kept a certain section of crowd and guests in mind and have created the menu. It's a success
Firstly it's fully vegetarian
Secondly the palate suits that section of crowd

This review of mine would b strictly on the basic of what the chef has created to cater too.

Started with Mexican Salad - could have been better ( chef please look into this ) found a bit off. Macaroni with mayonnaise and beans. Missed the punch, instead found it on a tad sweeter side.

Insalata Mista - Italian ( riso version ) fresh salad leaves crunchy , cherry tomatoes , cheese cubes , olives and dressed well with olive oil . Good . Served with garlic bread.

Beans Tacos - loved it . Refried beans with salsa , home made taco topped with grated processed cheese . Tangy sweet and spicy
Nicely presented served with salsa

Fungi Trifolati - not a mushroom fan but texture was nice . Had the glaze and sheen. Took a bite. Tasted good. Italian herbs does give that enhance taste. Healthy dish. Tossed mushrooms served with bread. Do try it out.

Must try the classic Fundue - enough for 2 served with veggies and toasted bread. This is basically a mix or blend of emmental and gruyere with a nice garlic punch. Nice texture and sheen.

These guys are known for their thin crust pizzas went for the spicy one called TOBACCO.
could have been more tangy and spicy but again it's all about the masses. Sun dried tomato and jalapeno played and enhanced the taste.

Lasagne and enchiladas have to be tried.Baked and served hot nicely stuffed. Enchiladas had cheese refried beans topped with Mexican sauce and Cheese. Good texture tasted good on the other hand I personally found the lasagne a bit dry ( chef please look into it )

Sizzler - Star dish of the day. SERVED PIPING HOT. spice level up to the mark. Rice tossed in chilli Sauce with a bit of schezwan and noodles with soy. Veggies with paneer had a good taste. This is one dish which is enough or 2 or a meal for one. Nice  combination

DESSERTS - not a fan but liked the chocolate mud cake.do try

Till we meet again
Cheers
